title: Ops Autopilot: Taskized Escalation Graph and Admin CLI Shim
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a lightweight adapter that converts authored escalation graphs (previously free-form runbooks) into task graphs that can be executed by the Ops Autopilot engine. Provide an opinionated Admin CLI shim for on-call engineers to trigger, inspect, and safely step through automated support flows. The goal is to reduce mean time to remediate for common incidents, make runbook actions auditable, and create safe manual overrides for automation.
acceptance_criteria: Authoring flow: YAML graph -> validated task graph with semantic checks
Admin CLI: start/stop/pause/resume a task graph with dry-run option
Observability: each task emits structured telemetry that appears in Console traces and cost breakdowns
Safety: default rate limits and activity-confirmation gates for destructive steps
Rollback: automated compensating steps and clear audit log entries for human overrides

implementation_notes: Adapter will reuse existing task-runner library from ENG-271443; extend it to support 'pause' and 'step' semantics.
Schema decision: use v1 YAML with explicit 'guards' to allow safe branching; validators implemented in TypeScript.
CLI will be a single binary (Go) that calls control-plane APIs; fallback to a web UI deep link for complex flows.
Telemetry: emit activity_id, task_id, actor, outcome, duration as tags for Console ingestion.
risks_mitigation: Risk: automation could execute destructive ops unintentionally. Mitigation: default safeties and require two-step confirmation for privileged actions.
Risk: schema drift between authored runbooks and runtime. Mitigation: strict validator and CI gating on PRs that change runbook files.
Risk: on-call cognitive load. Mitigation: provide 'dry-run' and 'explain' subcommands that show expected state changes.
Risk: telemetry volume. Mitigation: sample non-critical tasks and aggregate metrics for high-frequency flows.
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus on the guard semantics and the CLI confirmation UX during code review.
Telemetry fields are defined in implementation_notes; ensure Console ingest mapping exists before merge.
